title: Storage object and its support for indexed properties
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

I have become confused about Storage objects and their level of support for indexed properties. The answer based on WPT tests and what implementations do seems to be a bit different against the current specification.

Implementations and WPT support:

```
localStorage[9] = "some value"
```

As equivalent to:
```
localStorage.setItem("9", "some value");
```

https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#legacy-platform-object-set if given a number will fall back to OrdinarySetWithOwnDescriptor if that platform object does not [support indexed properties](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#dfn-support-indexed-properties).

However, this WPT test which every browser passes: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/be89ed1d0c8c1be3c4decb9165e9f1cad9c20949/webstorage/defineProperty.window.js#L54

Verifies that the number 9 is reflected in localStorage, which seems to indicate that Storage supports indexed properties.

Other WPT tests and browser behaviour indicates no support for indexed properties. For example: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/be89ed1d0c8c1be3c4decb9165e9f1cad9c20949/webstorage/storage_enumerate.window.js#L49

If Storage supports indexed properties then https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#legacy-platform-object-ownpropertykeys will additionally list the supported indexed properties. But in this case only the [named properties are listed](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/#the-storage-interface:supported-property-names).

Another test that I noticed which expects Storage not being indexed properties is https://wpt.fyi/results/webstorage/set.window.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned (all tests pass if that is the case), but there seems to be a difference between browser engines for that test.

Maybe I am just missed something here though, also happy to put up a MR to more concretely define the "determine the value of a named property" etc steps for the Storage object etc.
